plates.prompt: Create a landscape 4:3 literary engraving for Part I of The Thiele Machine, 'What keeping costs'. One end looms large in foreground; the matched cuts recede into shadow. An artisan's hand has withdrawn to the far edge; the retained marks remain sharply lit by a narrow high window. Gustave Dore style: extraordinary fine black-and-white wood engraving, deep shadows, white paper highlights, sublime scale with austere geometry. Show a vast extremely thin horizontal plane suspended in dark space, viewed obliquely from outside and somewhat above. A single enormous smooth sphere passes partly through that plane. The intersection is one clean ellipse in perspective, representing the circular section; only one sphere, only one plane. The sphere's upper rounded cap rises far above the plane and the lower curved part is visible beneath the front edge, making the three-dimensional geometry unmistakable. The plane is a clean unmarked surface, perhaps thin pale stone or paper, not a grid. The external reader can see the entire arrangement; this viewpoint is explicitly an outside view, not what a Flatlander would see. No humans or eyes standing up on the plane, no miniature buildings, no instruments, no portals. The conceptual subject is a section and what lies outside it. Dramatic oblique viewpoint; sphere shifted off centre, plane runs diagonally out of frame, huge atmospheric darkness. Carefully coherent sphere-plane intersection with no extra rings, seams or hole around the contact. Classic literary engraving, not 3D CAD, diagram or cosmic science-fiction scene. No stars, no magical rays, no text, no labels, no equations, no arrows, no signature or decorative frame. Monochrome black ink on ivory-white paper. Wide 4:3 composition.

Original Gustave Dore-style black-and-white wood engraving, exquisite fine crosshatching, profound shadow, broad readable composition. The actual subject is different windows admitting different views of one world; no single view shows everything.
